sum: Because the underlying ProShares Bitcoin ETF (BITO) will soon undergo a reverse stock split, its price index will be adjusted accordingly. To keep the Futures price aligned with the underlying asset, MEXC will rebase BITOUSDT Stock Futures during the adjustment window below. As part of the rebase, the number of contracts held and the corresponding entry price will be adjusted proportionally.
Adjustment Ratio = Price Index Before Adjustment / Price Index After Adjustment. The final adjustment ratio may fluctuate slightly due to real-time market conditions.

- The scheduled adjustment window is an estimate and may vary depending on actual progress. The actual resumption time will be subject to system execution. Please keep an eye on changes to your positions.

Example: Suppose you hold a 100-contract long position in BITOUSDT Stock Futures before the adjustment, with an average entry price of 90 USDT. The fair price at the time of adjustment is 60 USDT. Your account equity before unrealized PNL is 100,000 USDT.

- During the adjustment, existing BITOUSDT positions will be settled first, and new positions will be opened automatically once the adjustment is complete. However, if users have insufficient funds or market conditions are extremely volatile, existing positions may be settled without new positions being opened.

- During the adjustment, all trading bots (Grid, AI-powered, and Copy Trade) and strategies related to BITOUSDT will stop running. Trading bot strategies for BITOUSDT will not be restored once the rebase is complete and must be recreated by users. Only regular positions and Copy Trade positions will be restored after the adjustment according to the rules above.

5 Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) ETFs to Buy in 2026
sum: For investors, AI exchange-traded funds (ETFs) offer a simple way to get exposure to AI growth without relying on a single stock.

Artificial intelligence is no longer a futuristic concept. It's already shaping how companies operate and how consumers live. From recommendation engines and logistics software to chatbots and automation tools, AI is becoming a major driver of growth across tech, healthcare, finance, and other industries.

Rather than trying to pick individual winners, these funds group together companies that build AI technology or benefit from its adoption. That can include chipmakers, cloud platforms, software firms, and data-focused businesses.

Interest in AI investing remains strong as generative AI tools like ChatGPT push adoption into the mainstream. For investors seeking diversified exposure to AI’s long-term potential without the risk and research involved in picking individual stocks, AI ETFs can be a smart place to start.

Though the AI boom didn't begin in earnest until the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022, AI ETFs have been around for longer than that, with many investing in robotics, semiconductors, and related companies.

Among the top AI ETFs we'll look at in this article are the Global X Artificial Intelligence and Technology ETF, Global X Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF, Robo Global Robotics and Automation Index ETF, iShares Future AI and Tech ETF, and First Trust Nasdaq Artificial Intelligence and Robotics ETF.

Global X Artificial Intelligence and Technology ETF (AIQ -0.63%) is the largest AI ETF and a good first choice for investors looking for an AI ETF. The ETF launched in 2018 and aims to invest in companies that can benefit from the development of AI technology, as well as companies that make hardware used in AI, such as chips.

Asia chip stock sell-off hits 22 billionaires, wealth drops over $180 billion
sum: Huo Xing Finance reports that as the global sell-off in technology stocks spread to Asia, the fortunes of SoftBank Group founder Masayoshi Son and several other Asian business tycoons have significantly declined. Calculations show that by 10:00 AM Beijing time, the combined wealth of 22 billionaires from China, Japan, and South Korea—among the world’s 500 richest people—had initially dropped by more than $21 billion, later easing to over $18 billion. Son suffered the largest loss, with his personal wealth declining by $3.9 billion to approximately $29 billion. Companies at the heart of the AI boom were hit hardest. Billionaires whose wealth fell by at least $1 billion include TakeMitsu Takizaki, founder of Keyence, a manufacturer of electronic sensors, and Chang Chien-sheng, Singapore’s richest person and chairman of ASE Technology Holding. The family of Lee Jae-yong, a major shareholder of Samsung Electronics, along with his mother and sister, saw their combined wealth shrink by about $2.5 billion; the family is among Asia’s wealthiest.

A sharp sell-off in Asia’s chip stocks has erased over $180 billion in wealth for 22 billionaires from China, Japan, and South Korea, according to MarsBit. SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son saw his net worth drop by $3.9 billion to $29 billion, while Keyence’s Takeshi Yamaguchi and JCET’s Sunny Zhang also experienced significant declines. The crypto and tech markets’ Fear & Greed Index has turned sharply negative, with altcoins to watch showing mixed signals. Samsung’s Lee Jae-yong and his family lost approximately $2.5 billion as the sector-wide sell-off continues.

TraceParts joins KEYENCE Group
sum: On October 23, 2026, TraceParts joined KEYENCE Group, a global leader in the development and manufacturing of industrial automation and inspection equipment.

This transaction marks a new chapter in TraceParts’ development. By joining a global industrial group recognized for its technological expertise and ability to drive innovation, TraceParts aims to accelerate the development of its solutions and strengthen its ability to support component manufacturers and distributors, as well as the wider industrial community.
KEYENCE, a global leader in industrial automation and inspection equipment

Established in Japan in 1974, KEYENCE is now an innovative leader in the development and manufacturing of industrial automation and inspection equipment worldwide. Their products consist of code readers, laser markers, machine vision systems, measuring systems, microscopes, sensors, and static eliminators.
KEYENCE currently serves approximately 400,000 customers in 110 countries, operates 250 offices across 46 countries, and employs more than 12,000 people worldwide.
The Group generates approximately $7.3 billion in revenue and has achieved average annual growth of more than 10% over the past 25 years.
Innovation is at the heart of its strategy, with a strong ability to develop new technologies that address the needs of industrial companies.

items.t: Keyence (TSE:6861) Looks Fully Priced As Earnings, Dividend, And Split Draw Focus
sum: Keyence (TSE:6861) has thrown several big headlines at investors at once, including a stock split tied to changes in its Articles of Incorporation and a richer interim dividend.
Those governance moves arrive alongside half year figures that show higher sales, net income, and earnings per share compared with the same period a year earlier.

Keyence’s governance and dividend moves are landing while the share price sits at ¥78,000, after a 2.15% 1-day share price return but a 30-day share price return that is down 3.94%. This hints that enthusiasm has cooled even as the year-to-date share price return of 36.41% and 1-year total shareholder return of 37.18% keep longer term momentum intact.

Keyence has just paired rapid profit expansion with a richer dividend and a stock split at a trailing P/E of 34.8x. Is most of the rerating already in the price, or is it not yet reflected?
Keyence is trading at a P/E of 34.8x, which is rich compared with both its sector and peer group, even after the recent share price cooling to ¥78,000.

The P/E ratio compares the current share price to earnings per share and helps you see how much investors are paying for each unit of profit. For a profitable automation specialist like Keyence, this metric often reflects how much faith the market has in future cash generation and the durability of its earnings profile.

The robot boom is bigger than humanoids: mapping the companies behind it
sum: - Humanoids are the headline, but robotics already spans factories, warehouses, vision systems, motion control and artificial intelligence.
- Nvidia, Cognex, Fanuc and specialist component makers provide very different ways to gain exposure to the same theme.
- The key question is not only which robot wins, but which parts of the value chain remain scarce and valuable.
Robots can already dance. Investors appear equally capable of getting excited about it.

China's Unitree surged nearly sixfold on its Shanghai debut on 19 August, briefly valuing the humanoid robot maker at around 50 billion USD. The listing coincides with Beijing's World Robot Conference, where hundreds of companies are displaying everything from industrial machines to humanoid robots.

Unitree makes a useful hook, but it is not the whole investment story. Humanoids remain early, and relatively few perform productive commercial work today. The broader opportunity is what happens when artificial intelligence gives existing robots better brains, eyes and decision-making abilities.
For investors, that means looking underneath the robot's skin.

Nikkei 225 Outlook Weakens as Chicago Futures Slide and Semiconductor Stocks Weigh
sum: The Tokyo stock market is expected to open with a weak tone on the 28th. Following the decline in tech and semiconductor stocks in the U.S. market the previous day, artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor-related issues are likely to act as a drag on the index in Tokyo. The fact that the yen-denominated settlement price of Chicago Nikkei futures fell significantly below the Osaka exchange settlement price is also expected to add to selling pressure in the morning session.
The forecast range is between 63,800 and 64,500, with a high probability of trading below the 27th closing level of 64,931.19.

In the U.S. stock market on the 27th, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite and the SOX (Philadelphia Semiconductor) Index fell. Following this trend, AI and semiconductor-related stocks, which have a high contribution to the Nikkei 225, are likely to face early selling pressure in Tokyo. The foreign exchange market is trading almost flat from the previous day, with the dollar around the upper 163-yen range and the euro in the lower 186-yen range.

In the yen-converted values of ADRs (American Depositary Receipts) on the 27th, Kioxia (285A.T), Furukawa Electric (5801.T), and Sumitomo Electric (5802.T) closed below their Tokyo closing prices, suggesting a weak start for these issues in the cash market. The yen-denominated settlement price of Chicago Nikkei futures was 64,055, down 1,115 points compared to the Osaka exchange settlement.

In the Tokyo market on the previous day, the 27th, buying initially led on hopes for calm in the Middle East, but the market was subsequently pushed down by selling on rallies. Early trading saw positive sentiment driven by a retreat in geopolitical risk after a large-scale U.S. attack on Iran was avoided and Iran announced it would halt retaliatory strikes. However, the buying did not last, and following the decline in semiconductor-related stocks in the U.S. market on the 24th, selling dominated, particularly in AI-related names. The Nikkei 225 fell to 64,321.57 at 10:07 a.m., down 289.58 points from the previous weekend.
By sector, non-ferrous metals, mining, pharmaceuticals, glass and ceramics, and chemicals declined.

items.t: Japan's Nikkei closes above 60,000 for first time on earnings optimism
sum: Japan's Nikkei closed above the key 60,000 mark for the first time today as optimism over corporate earnings overshadowed concerns about the Middle East conflict.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 Index rose 1.38% to finish the session at an unprecedented 60,537. The Nikkei has gained 18.6% so far this year.

Shares of factory automation provider Keyence and industrial robot maker Fanuc surged by their daily trading limit, nearly 16%, to lead gains in the Nikkei after both firms reported better-than-expected profit after the bell on Friday.
"Stocks related to earnings announcements, as well as AI and semiconductor-related shares, led the market higher at the open," said Maki Sawada, an equities strategist at Nomura Securities.
"This week will see a steady stream of earnings reports from major companies in both Japan and the US, so market attention will naturally gravitate toward those results," the strategist said.
"Since 60,000 is a psychological milestone, many investors are likely keeping an eye on that level, so profit-taking could manifest around that range," she added.

The Nikkei fell into negative territory shortly after the open, but then rallied sharply following an Axios report that Iran has given the US a new proposal to end their war. Discussions to settle the two-month-long conflict were stalled over the weekend.
